pr_title: Bluetooth: Audio: Add PACS for broadcast sink
pr_body:
Add support for using PACS and/or capabilities for
the broadcast sink role. PACS and capabilities were
originally only supported for the unicast server
role, so the PACS callbacks were moved their own
struct, as if a device supports both the unicast
server role and the broadcast sink role, it will
only have a single PACS instance.

Signed-off-by: Emil Gydesen <emil.gydesen@nordicsemi.no>

fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/43788
pr_comments: @MariuszSkamra can you please take a look?

issue_context.title: LE Audio: Broadcast Sink shall instantiate PACS
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
From the BAP spec: 
> The Broadcast Sink shall instantiate one Published Audio Capabilities Service.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Broadcast Sink shall `select` PACS. 
The PACS callbacks shall somehow work with the broadcast sink callbacks as well. We need to figure out how this will work together with the PACS callbacks for the unicast server when a device supports both roles. 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
N/A

**Additional context**
N/A

review_comments:
I wonder if `pref` should be moved to a unicast server-only struct since it has no value for the broadcast sink. 

Somewhat the same with the `ops` as those are only used for the unicast server, but the broadcast sink could be refactored to use some of them (except that the broadcast sink always works on a group, and not individual streams).

Each BIS is an individual stream I guess and an BASS-client can dynamically instruct a receiver to sync to one or more BISes - hence the application needs to be able to handle individual BIS LC3 start/stop + cleanup.
Don't think it needs to be part of this PR though, unless it is easier? (Not sure how it works today from an API perspective - maybe this is already supported)

These are the `struct bt_audio_capability_ops`, which are used by the unicast server for stream configuration. 

The `struct bt_audio_stream_ops` still has the `started` and `stopped` callbacks for the broadcast sink role.

Maybe outside of this PR, so possibly make a note of it.
Does this call notify a change of the locations, or just of the direction of the location?  In the latter case, the name is probably confusing.
Just wondering what prompted you to change from the IS_ENABLED to #if defined here

The Kconfig `CONFIG_BT_PACS_SNK_CONTEXT` is guarded by `CONFIG_BT_PAC_SNK`:
```c
if BT_PAC_SRC
config BT_PACS_SRC_CONTEXT
	hex "Supported Source Contexts"
	default 0x03ff
	range 0x0000 0x03ff
```

So we won't be able to use it unless `CONFIG_BT_PAC_SNK` is enabled (`IS_ENABLED` does not work for guarded Kconfigs)
